analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet Hotels is a quality hospitality asset owner benefiting from India's travel boom, with operating CF surging to ₹950 Cr in FY25 and revenue nearly tripling from pandemic lows. However, at ₹17,080 Cr market cap, 28x P/E, D/E of 0.73, and ROE of only 5.77%, it is too large, too expensive, and too capital-hungry to fit the SMILE framework.
key_strengths: Strong operating cash flow recovery — OCF ₹950 Cr in FY25, up from ₹62 Cr in FY22; 5/5 positive OCF years
Premium hotel locations with high operating margins (35.5% EBIT margin) showing real pricing power
Promoter holding at 67.3% with equity base doubled to ₹3,415 Cr in FY25 via capital raise, reducing debt from ₹3,005 Cr to ₹2,489 Cr
key_risks: D/E of 0.73 exceeds my 0.6 red-flag threshold; ₹2,489 Cr debt against ₹765 Cr EBITDA still constrains returns
Massive capex spike to ₹969 Cr in FY25 (up from ₹436 Cr) flipped FCF to -₹14 Cr — asset-heavy expansion destroys near-term free cash
ROE of 5.77% is dangerously low for a P/B of 5x; net profit of ₹142 Cr in FY25 actually fell from ₹278 Cr in FY24 despite revenue growth
red_flags: Market cap ₹17,080 Cr — 17x outside my sweet spot of ≤₹1,000 Cr
P/E 28.2x exceeds my 20x hard limit for small-cap value investing
D/E 0.73 breaches the 0.6 threshold; hotel assets are illiquid collateral in a downturn
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Chalet operates premium business hotels (upscale, Marriott/Westin-branded properties) in gateway cities — a structurally sound business riding India's corporate travel and MICE boom. Revenue CAGR of 12.8% over 9 years and EBITDA CAGR of 14% look decent, but net profit has been deeply erratic (losses in 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022) reflecting the leverage-heavy model. The FY23–24 profit recovery was real but FY25 net profit dropped back to ₹142 Cr even as EBITDA hit ₹765 Cr — testament to high interest and depreciation drag.

The ₹969 Cr capex in FY25 signals aggressive expansion but at this market cap and P/E, the market has already priced in the story. For a stock to be a multibagger from ₹17,000 Cr, it would need to become a ₹85,000+ Cr company — possible but requires flawless execution and multiple re-ratings. With ROE barely above 5%, I cannot justify paying 5x book. This is a mid-cap institutional play, not a SMILE multibagger.
